steps.body: Run the shortcuts backward: a monic quadratic with roots r and s is **x² − (sum)x + (product)**. Roots 3 ± 2i: sum 6, product 9 + 4 = 13, so the quadratic is **x² − 6x + 13**. Note the sign: minus the sum.

options.label: x² + 6x + 13
options.feedback: The middle term is MINUS the sum: −(+6)x = −6x.

options.label: x² − 6x + 5
options.feedback: 9 − 4 subtracts — the product of conjugates is 9 + 4 = 13.

options.label: x² − 6x − 13
options.feedback: A conjugate-pair product a² + b² is always POSITIVE: +13.

steps.body: This is also why complex roots of real quadratics **must** come in conjugate pairs: only then do the sum (2a) and product (a² + b²) come out real. One root 4 − i immediately tells you the other is 4 + i.

commonBuilds.feedback: Minus the sum: the middle term is −2x.

widget.prompt: One root of a real-coefficient quadratic is 4 − i. What is the PRODUCT of both roots?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is the SUM (4 + 4) — the product is a² + b² = 17.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The other root is 4 + i; product = 16 + 1 = 17.

explanationVariants: Roots 4 ± i: sum 8, product 17, so x² − 8x + 17.
The conjugate 4 + i completes the pair; assemble x² − (sum)x + (product).

widget.prompt: A real-coefficient monic quadratic has 4 − i as a root. Which is it?

commonBuilds.feedback: Sign slip. The middle coefficient is minus the sum of the roots: (4−i)+(4+i) = 8, so the term is −8x.
The sum counts BOTH roots: 4 + 4 = 8, so the middle term is −8x.

widget.missFeedback: The conjugate pair 4 ± i sums to 8 (→ −8x) and multiplies to 16 + 1 = 17.
widget.successFeedback: Right — the pair 4 ± i has sum 8 and product 17.

explanationVariants: Substitute and watch everything cancel — the build is exact.

options.label: yes — (1 + i)² = 2i, and 2i − (2 + 2i) + 2 = 0
options.feedback: Right — the terms cancel to exactly 0.

options.label: no — (1 + i)² = 2, and 2 − 2 − 2i + 2 = 2 − 2i
options.feedback: (1 + i)² = 1 + 2i + i² = 2i, not 2 — with that, everything cancels.

options.label: no — complex numbers can't satisfy real equations
options.feedback: They can — substitution plus i² = −1 closes the check at 0.

options.label: yes — because 1 + i is the conjugate of 1 − i
options.feedback: Being a conjugate isn't the check — SUBSTITUTION is: (1 + i)² − 2(1 + i) + 2 = 0. ✓

steps.body: Same center, different spread — what actually moves?
explanationVariants: Both pairs share real part −1, so the sum is −2 for each — the x-coefficient (+2x) can't change. Only the product a² + b² sees the imaginary part: 1 + 4 = 5 for A, 1 + 16 = 17 for B.
The middle term is set entirely by the real part; the constant term is the only place the imaginary magnitude shows up.

widget.prompt: Quadratic A has roots −1 ± 2i. Quadratic B has roots −1 ± 4i. Which part of x² − (sum)x + (product) is DIFFERENT between A and B?

options.label: the x-coefficient only
options.feedback: Both pairs share the same real part, −1, so the sum (−2) — and the x-coefficient it sets — is identical for A and B. Look at the constant instead.

options.label: the constant term only
options.feedback: Right — the sum only depends on the real part (−1 for both, giving +2x either way), but the product a² + b² grows with the imaginary part: 1 + 4 = 5 for A, 1 + 16 = 17 for B.

options.label: both the x-coefficient and the constant term
options.feedback: The x-coefficient stays put — it's set only by the real part, and both pairs share real part −1. Only the constant term moves.

options.label: neither — A and B are the same quadratic
options.feedback: They share an x-coefficient (+2x) but not a constant: A's product is 1 + 4 = 5, B's is 1 + 16 = 17. Different quadratics.

hints: Find the sum for each pair first: (−1+2i)+(−1−2i) and (−1+4i)+(−1−4i).
Both sums are −2 — so the x-coefficient −(−2)x = +2x is locked in for both.
Now the products: 1² + 2² = 5 for A, but 1² + 4² = 17 for B. That's the one that moves.

steps.body: x² − (sum)x + (product) rebuilds the quadratic from any conjugate pair.
takeaways: Sum 2a → middle term −2a·x; product a² + b² → constant.
One complex root of a real quadratic reveals the other: its conjugate.
Verify builds by substitution — the cancellation is exact.
steps.teaser: Last lesson: with four solving methods on the table, learn to pick the fastest.

concept.body: Roots 1 ± i: sum 2, product 1 + 1 = 2. The quadratic is x² − (sum)x + (product).

options.label: x² + 2x + 2
options.feedback: The middle term is MINUS the sum: −2x.

options.label: x² − 2x
options.feedback: The product 1 + 1 = 2 is the constant term — it can't be dropped.
